turnaround_reason: Charter has been crushed (from ~$286 to ~$149, a fresh 52-week low) as broadband subscriber losses accelerated to ~172K in a quarter under fixed-wireless and fiber assault. The bull case rests on the $34.5B Cox merger closing and a huge, cheap free-cash-flow base.
bullish_points: Extremely cheap on cash flow: fwd P/E ~3.4, EV/EBITDA ~5.4, ~$2.2B FCF
$34.5B Cox acquisition expected to close, adding ~6.5M customers and ~$800M operating synergies
12M+ mobile lines is a genuine growth vector cross-selling into the broadband base
Management expects Cox scale plus network upgrades to improve internet unit trajectory
Street mean target (~$184) implies meaningful upside from a washed-out price
bearish_points: Core broadband is in secular decline -- 172K sub losses and management warns competition stays 'fierce'
Balance sheet is heavy: debt/equity ~441, current ratio 0.36; the Cox deal adds more leverage
Cord-cutting continues to erode legacy video
Fixed wireless (T-Mobile/Verizon) and fiber overbuilders are structural, not cyclical, headwinds
'Cheap on FCF' is the classic value-trap profile if the FCF base itself is eroding
catalyst: Cox merger close plus a quarter showing broadband net-adds stabilizing (losses narrowing)
catalyst_timing: Merger close expected summer/H2 2026; Q3 earnings ~2026-10-30
suggested_trade: Small starter spot only near the 52-week low; scale only if a quarter shows broadband losses decelerating. Not a size-up until the sub bleed slows.
key_risk: Broadband subscriber losses keep accelerating, making the low multiple a melting-ice-cube rather than a bargain.
would_skip_if: Next print shows sub losses widening again or the Cox deal timeline slips/adds worse-than-expected leverage.
